source_text.body:
Search years of Gmail and build a timeline with Grok Bot
A commenter had Grok Bot search five years of their email and produce a timeline; the poster wants to use it to organize a large Gmail inbox.
·
Oct 30, 2026
Done with
GB
Grok Bot
What they did
In the thread, one commenter said Grok Bot searched five years of their email after a board meeting and built a timeline showing how long a topic had been revisited without a decision. Other commenters described broader Gmail setups where Grok Bot was connected to the inbox, then used to sort and label mail, unsubscribe from newsletters, archive or delete messages, and keep monitoring the inbox with periodic summaries.
How it went
People in the thread reported outcomes like cleaning 10,000 unread emails, deleting thousands of messages, and finding duplicate HBO billing. The main limitation discussed was risk: commenters advised using labels, archive, dry runs, and approval before bulk deletes because mistakes are possible.
Worth knowing
One practical catch from the thread: Gmail Trash keeps deleted mail for 30 days, so using archive first or checking a dry run gives you a recovery window.
Try it yourself
with
Grok Bot
Copy prompt
Connect to my Gmail with read-only access and search the last [number] years for everything about [topic, person, or project]. Build a chronological timeline in markdown with date, sender, subject, and a one-line summary of each key event, and flag anything that looks unresolved. Don't delete, archive, label, or send anything. You're done when I have the timeline file and a short list of open items.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/GrokBot/comments/1xfzqtz/thoughts_on_using_grok_bot_to_organise_my_main
